Looking at this question about the Ingraham 2022 protein design paper and how symmetry was enforced in protein complexes with respect to a specific space group.

In diffusion-based protein design, enforcing symmetry constraints can be done in several ways. The key approach in the Ingraham 2022 work involved modifying the sampling procedure of the diffusion process itself. Rather than using external classifiers, VAEs, or traditional docking protocols, they analytically conditioned the stochastic/ordinary differential equation (SDE/ODE) that governs the reverse diffusion process to respect the desired symmetry group. This means at each step of the denoising/sampling procedure, the dynamics were modified to be symmetric with respect to the space group operations - an analytical way of enforcing the constraint directly in the mathematical formulation of the sampling process.

This approach (symmetric sampling of the SDE/ODE) is distinct from:
- Classifier-free guidance (which uses additional score terms)
- VAE conditioning (which uses a learned encoder/decoder)
- Rosetta docking (a completely different methodology)

[ANSWER]E[/ANSWER]
